brief: Zero Hedge relays a Goldman commodities note from Yulia Zhestkova Grigsby and Daan Struyven that revises Persian Gulf tanker-flow estimates sharply higher. Visible tanker data show only 10mb/d on a seven-day average, but accounting for dark transits Goldman puts actual Gulf exports at 15-16mb/d, about two-thirds of pre-war levels. The 5mb/d gap comes from tankers crossing near the Omani coast with AIS transponders switched off to avoid Iranian detection, which is also the source of a 5mb/d upward revision over two weeks. Goldman therefore estimates the net hit to Gulf flows at 7.9mb/d, smaller than visible shipping data implied, and infers visible data understate stocks by 39mb, implying 2.1mb/d of inventory draws over 30 days. Brent has risen to $95 as markets price a no-deal status quo for longer. Goldman says renewed US-Iran strikes and at least six tanker attacks in 10 days keep oil infrastructure at risk, while rising dark transits and price-sensitive Chinese buying should cap crude upside absent large infrastructure damage. Red Sea exports fell 4.5mb/d in August as Saudi Arabia redirected Yanbu flows east. Zero Hedge adds that middle-distillate tightness remains unresolved.
